connections.why: Weimar and Nazi Germany are a focal case study in the twentieth-century clash of ideologies
German unification in 1871 sets the long-run context for the German state studied from 1919
The Russian Revolution launches the communist ideology central to Europe's ideological struggle
Fascist Italy is a key strand in the twentieth-century contest of ideologies
Italian unification by 1871 is the springboard for Italy's quest for great-power status
The 1823–67 Irish material sits inside the longer Act of Union narrative (mutually excluded as a choice for this reason)
Nineteenth-century nationalism and Home Rule lead toward the partition of Ireland
The breakdown of the Union culminates in partition by 1925
The Williamite settlement frames the Protestant Ascendancy challenged in the 1798 era
The 1801 Union created by the 1798 crisis is what eventually fractures into partition
Early-Stuart conflict is the opening phase of the Crown–Parliament struggle to 1714
Henrician and mid-Tudor England lead directly into the Elizabethan settlement
The Elizabethan inheritance shapes the tensions that erupt under the early Stuarts
Bourbon absolutism under Louis XIV sets the backdrop for France's search for stable government after 1815
Nineteenth-century French ambitions feed the great-power rivalries that culminate in war
Italy's pursuit of status is part of the great-power competition driving European conflict
Both options trace the development of representative government and political reform over time
Tudor England and Habsburg Spain are intertwined through the reign of Mary I and Philip II
Nazi Germany is central to the consequences of great-power conflict to 1945
Both are early-twentieth-century studies of revolution, partition and the making of new states
